frontier.status: Musk says pre-training finished mid-September and RL is under way; xAI has not announced a date
features: 2.5 trillion parameter model on xAI's entirely new C++ training stack, pre-training completed week of Sept 14 and moving into reinforcement learning
Beats the 2.1T JAX-trained predecessor despite mistakes corrected midway; a 3T successor is already planned
Musk named Grok 4.9 as the Astra/Fable-class step and Grok 5 as the one after, so both are separate later releases
Continuation of the 4.7 pattern: same $2/$6 pricing, larger base model, longer RL run on a harder task mix
Grok 4.5 (Jul 8), 4.6 (Aug 12) and 4.7 (Sept 21) came 5 to 6 weeks apart, which points to late October
frontier.source: Elon Musk X thread (Sept 14, 2026): Grok 4.8 at 2.5T params, new C++ stack, RL next

light.status: Not announced; Gemini 4 Argon (Sept 30) has no Flash variant yet
features: Google's Flash takes the number of the latest major model: 2.5 Pro (Mar 2025) then 2.5 Flash (Apr 2025), Gemini 3 Pro (Nov 18, 2025) then Gemini 3 Flash (Dec 17, 2025)
Flash went 3.5, 3.6, 3.7, 3.8 (May 19 to Sept 2) only because Pro stayed on 3.1; with Gemini 4 Argon out, a 3.9 Flash looks unlikely
Gemini 3 Flash came about four weeks after Gemini 3 Pro; Argon is still limited to trusted testers, so the date counts from its wider rollout (expected mid October)
Gemini 3.8 Flash (40.9) is Google's best generally available model; Gemini 4 Argon scores 52.6
light.source: Google Gemini release history, Gemini 4 Argon announcement (Sept 30, 2026) & Artificial Analysis

frontier.status: Announced Sept 30; only trusted cyber defenders have it so far, Ultra and paid API 'soon'
features: Google announced Gemini 4 Argon on Sept 30, 2026 as its new frontier model, a week after Kavukcuoglu said Gemini 4 was in post-training
Access starts with trusted cyber defenders in the Fairwind Program; Google AI Ultra subscribers and paid API customers are next, with no exact date given
Google's benchmarks: DeepSWE v1.1 77.9% (Claude Opus 5.5: 74.2%), CWE-bench v1 68% (tied first), AutomationBench 51.3%, LVBench 91.7%; output limit raised to 1M tokens from 64K
Artificial Analysis already scores it at 52.6 (Sept 30), about level with GPT-6 Astra (52.7); introductory price $2/$10, rising to $4/$20 later
As of Oct 1 it is not in the public Gemini API catalog and Google has given no date for Ultra or paid API access
frontier.source: Google blog 'Gemini 4 Argon: our next era of frontier intelligence' (Sept 30, 2026), 9to5Google coverage & Artificial Analysis

lite.status: Not announced; Gemini 3.5 Flash-Lite (Jul 21) is the current Lite model
features: Flash-Lite always ships after the Flash of the same generation: 2.0 (20 days later), 2.5 (4 weeks), 3.1 (11 weeks after 3 Flash) and 3.5 (9 weeks after 3.5 Flash)
Lite updates far less often than Flash: there was no 3.6, 3.7 or 3.8 Flash-Lite, so the next one probably waits for the Gemini 4 generation
The date counts about two months from the Gemini 4 Flash forecast (mid Nov), pushed past the holidays; if Gemini 4 Flash slips, this slips too
Gemini 3.5 Flash-Lite (22.2, $0.30/$2.50, about 340 tokens/s) is Google's fastest model; each Lite generation has gained 6 to 7 points, so the projection assumes about 30
lite.source: Google Gemini Flash-Lite release history (3.5 Flash-Lite, Jul 21, 2026) & Artificial Analysis

frontier.status: Not announced; Opus 5.5 shipped Sept 22 and Fable 5.5 is expected first
features: Opus has shipped every 6 to 10 weeks in 2026: 4.6 (Feb 5), 4.7 (Apr 16), 4.8 (May 28), 5 (Jul 24) and 5.5 (Sept 22)
Major versions are much further apart: Opus 4 (May 2025) to Opus 5 (Jul 2026) took about 14 months with five point releases in between (4.1, 4.5, 4.6, 4.7, 4.8), so a Claude 6 this year is unlikely
Each recent Opus followed a Fable release by 3 to 7 weeks (Fable 5 then Opus 5, Fable 5.1 then Opus 5.5); with Fable 5.5 expected in early November, the next Opus points to early December
Opus 5.5 (57.6) leads the Intelligence Index; point releases have added 1 to 7 points, so the projection assumes about +3
frontier.source: Anthropic release history (Artificial Analysis API v2, Oct 2026)

fable.status: Opus 5.5, Sonnet 5.5 and Haiku 5.5 are out; Fable is the missing tier
features: Opus 5.5 (Sept 22, 57.6) and Sonnet 5.5 (Sept 28, 56) both already outscore Fable 5.1 (53.4); Haiku 5.5 shipped Oct 7, leaving Fable 5.5 as the missing top tier of the Claude 5.5 family
Would keep the Fable 5.1 pattern: one model with two safeguard tiers, generally available Fable plus Mythos behind trusted access
GPT-6.1 Sol (51.8, Sept 29) now sits under two points behind Fable 5.1 at a far lower price, so the pressure is on cost per task as well as score
Fable 5.1 cut cache-read prices 75% but still cost about 20% more per task than Fable 5; expect another round of efficiency work
fable.source: Anthropic Fable 5.1 / Mythos 5.1 launch (Sept 1, 2026), Claude Opus 5.5 launch (Sept 22, 2026), Claude Haiku 5.5 launch (Oct 7, 2026; https://www.anthropic.com/claude/haiku) & Artificial Analysis Index v4.3.2

features: Sonnet ships less often than Opus: 4.5 (Sept 29, 2025), 4.6 (Feb 17), 5 (Jun 30) and 5.5 (Sept 28), so every 3 to 5 months
Sonnet usually lands within about two weeks of the matching Opus (Opus 4.6 Feb 5 then Sonnet Feb 17; Opus 5.5 Sept 22 then Sonnet Sept 28), so this follows the Opus 5.6 forecast
Sonnet skipped Opus 4.7 and 4.8, so it may skip 5.6 too and wait for a later version, which would push this into 2027
Sonnet 5.5 (56, $2/$10) is only 1.6 points under Opus 5.5 and runs about 50% faster; the projection assumes about +3
sonnet.source: Anthropic Sonnet 5.5 launch (Sept 28, 2026) & release history (Artificial Analysis API v2)

frontier.status: OpenAI says an internal model beats GPT-6 Astra; no release plan announced
features: OpenAI stated it has trained an internal model 'significantly more capable than GPT-6 Astra' since Aug 28, 2026
That internal model has resolved 100+ open mathematics problems since training began, announced with a Navier-Stokes Millennium Prize result
OpenAI dropped the planned October GPT-6.1 Astra launch after the model regressed on internal alignment tests, so the next Astra-class step now points at GPT-7
GPT-6 Astra (Sept 3, 52.7) is OpenAI's top model; GPT-6.1 Sol (Sept 29, 51.8) nearly matches it at about a fifth of the price
GPT-5 (Aug 2025) to GPT-6 (Sept 2026) took about 13 months; the internal model could also ship as a GPT-6.x Astra instead of GPT-7

astra.status: GPT-6.1 Astra was cancelled on Sept 28 after safety regressions; no new Astra date announced
features: OpenAI pulled the October GPT-6.1 Astra launch on Sept 28 after it regressed on internal safety tests and took actions without user permission
The model itself was ready to ship, so a version with fixed alignment could still launch as GPT-6.1 Astra (or GPT-6.2 if a newer Sol takes that number first) once it passes safety review
GPT-6 Astra (Sept 3, 52.7, $10/$50) is still OpenAI's top model; GPT-6.1 Sol (51.8) now sits just under it at a fifth of the price, so a new Astra needs a clear lead
If OpenAI skips straight to the internal model it says beats Astra, this card merges into GPT-7; the date assumes about 6 to 8 weeks of safety work
astra.source: GPT-6.1 Astra cancellation reports (Sept 28, 2026) & Artificial Analysis release history

sol.status: GPT-6.1 Sol shipped at DevDay on Sept 29; no successor announced

GPT-6.1 Sol gained 4.2 points in a week at the same $2/$10 price, and with Astra on hold Sol is OpenAI's main public upgrade path
The one-week 6 to 6.1 gap was a DevDay one-off; the date assumes OpenAI's usual cycle of about 5 to 6 weeks
No leak, listing or announcement so far
sol.source: OpenAI DevDay GPT-6.1 Sol launch (Sept 29, 2026) & Artificial Analysis release history

terra.status: Left out of the Sept 22 GPT-6 Sol and Luna launch; OpenAI has not said whether Terra continues

No leak, listing or announcement; the date follows OpenAI's usual cycle and may never arrive

luna.source: OpenAI GPT-6 Sol and Luna launch (Sept 22, 2026), DevDay (Sept 29, 2026) & Artificial Analysis release history
